title: The classic architectures: ResNet, EfficientNet, and what each one changed

videos.script: In 1998, a small network read the handwritten numbers on bank cheques. {{lenet}} It had convolutions, pooling, and a dense layer at the end. Most networks since then changed one thing about the one before. {{table}} This lesson follows those changes, one at a time, and measures each of them. VGG replaced large filters with stacks of small ones. {{stack}} Two three-by-three filters see what one five-by-five sees, and cost less. Then networks got deeper, and something odd happened. {{curves}} Past a certain depth, they trained worse, even on their own training images. You will see it on the digits. At twenty layers, the loss never moves. {{flat}} ResNet fixed it with one addition. Each block adds its input back to its output. {{block}} The gradient then reaches the first layers, and twenty layers train. {{grads}} After that, the question became cost. {{split}} MobileNet splits each convolution into two cheap ones. EfficientNet grows depth, width and image size together, by one rule. {{scaling}} Nothing here is downloaded. Every network is built from its code, with random weights. {{empty}} By the end, you can read an architecture by what it changed, and choose one. {{end}}
